i: 처음 만났을 때와 헤어질 때 하는 아주 쉬운 인사입니다.
Very easy greetings for when you meet someone for the first time and when you say goodbye.
w: I say hello with a smile.
I say hello in the morning.
f: I'm Sam. Nice to meet you.
처음 만나서 기쁠 때 하는 인사
How have you been? (after a long time)
Long time no see. How have you been?
tp: "안녕하세요?" is used in the morning, afternoon and evening, any time. It is like "Hello" in English.
"안녕하세요?" can be used in the morning, afternoon and evening. It is like "Hello".
가는 사람에게는 "안녕히 가세요", 남는 사람에게는 "안녕히 계세요"라고 합니다.
To the person leaving, say "안녕히 가세요"; to the person staying, say "안녕히 계세요".
dl: to be well, to be at peace
Hello. I'm Minha. Nice to meet you.
to be well, to be at peace
sm: 만나면 "안녕하세요?", 헤어질 때는 "안녕히 가세요" 또는 "안녕히 계세요"라고 합니다.
When you meet, say "안녕하세요?"; when you part, say "안녕히 가세요" or "안녕히 계세요".
qz: 내가 먼저 갑니다. 남는 사람에게 하는 인사는?

i: 고마울 때, 미안할 때 하는 말과 그 대답입니다.
Words for saying thank you and sorry, and how to answer them.
w: I buy a gift for my friend.
f: I'm sorry. I'll do it again.
Excuse me. May I come in?
Excuse me. Where is the restroom?
tp: 윗사람에게는 "감사합니다", "죄송합니다"를 씁니다.
To older people or people above you, use "감사합니다" and "죄송합니다".
"감사합니다"의 대답은 "아니에요", "죄송합니다"의 대답은 "괜찮아요"입니다.
The answer to "감사합니다" is "아니에요", and the answer to "죄송합니다" is "괜찮아요".
sm: 고마우면 "감사합니다", 미안하면 "죄송합니다"라고 합니다.
When you are thankful, say "감사합니다"; when you are sorry, say "죄송합니다".

i: 이름과 나이를 묻고 답하는 쉬운 말입니다.
Easy words for asking and answering about names and age.
w: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to be well, to be at peace
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
How old is your younger brother or sister?
tp: "씨"는 다른 사람 이름 뒤에만 붙입니다. 내 이름에는 붙이지 않습니다.
"씨" goes only after other people's names. Don't use it with your own name.
나이는 "스무 살, 서른 살"처럼 "살"을 붙여 말합니다.
For age, add "살", like "스무 살 (20 years old), 서른 살 (30 years old)".
sm: 이름은 "이름이 뭐예요?", 나이는 "몇 살이에요?"로 묻습니다.
Ask a name with "이름이 뭐예요?" and age with "몇 살이에요?".
qz: 맞는 것은? 저는 샘 씨예요 / 저는 샘이에요

i: 어느 나라 사람인지, 무슨 말을 하는지 말하는 쉬운 말입니다.
Easy words for saying which country you are from and which language you speak.
w: It's my first time in Korea.
to try, to have done (-아/어 보다)
tp: 나라 이름 뒤에 "사람"을 붙이면 그 나라 사람, "어"를 붙이면 그 나라 말입니다.
Add "사람" after a country name = a person from that country; add "어" = that country's language: 한국 사람 (Korean person), 한국어 (Korean language).
sm: "어느 나라 사람이에요?"에는 "미얀마 사람이에요"처럼 답합니다.
Answer "어느 나라 사람이에요?" with "미얀마 사람이에요" (I'm from Myanmar).

i: 대답하는 말과, 못 알아들었을 때 쓰는 말입니다. 처음 일할 때 가장 필요한 말입니다.
Words for answering and for when you didn't understand. These are the most needed words when you start somewhere new.
w: to be right, to be correct
to know (알겠어요 = I understand, got it)
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to try, to have done (-아/어 보다)
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to be right, to be correct
f: Got it. I'll do it right away.
I don't know, I don't understand
I'm sorry, but please say it again.
tp: 못 알아들었는데 "네"라고 하면 수업이나 아르바이트에서 문제가 생길 수 있습니다. 모르면 꼭 다시 물어보세요.
If you say "네" when you didn't understand, there can be problems in class or at your part-time job. If you don't understand, always ask again.
말이 빠르면 "천천히 말해 주세요"라고 부탁하세요.
If someone speaks fast, ask: "천천히 말해 주세요" (Please speak slowly).
dl: I'm sorry, but please say it again.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
sm: 모르면 "다시 말해 주세요", 알면 "알겠습니다"라고 합니다.
If you don't understand, say "다시 말해 주세요"; if you understand, say "알겠습니다".
qz: I don't know, I don't understand

i: 기분이나 느낌을 한마디로 말하는 쉬운 말입니다.
Easy words for saying how you feel in one word.
f: Are you tired? Take a rest.
I've been hungry since the morning.
Are you cold? Shall I close the door?
tp: 앞에 "정말", "너무", "조금"을 붙이면 느낌이 얼마나 큰지 말할 수 있습니다.
Put "정말 (really)", "너무 (so, too)" or "조금 (a little)" in front to say how strong the feeling is.
끝을 올려 말하면 묻는 말이 됩니다. "피곤해요?", "맛있어요?"
Raise your voice at the end to make it a question: "피곤해요?" (Are you tired?), "맛있어요?" (Is it delicious?).
sm: 느낌은 "좋아요", "피곤해요"처럼 한마디로 말합니다. 끝을 올리면 묻는 말입니다.
Say your feelings in one word, like "좋아요", "피곤해요". If your voice goes up at the end, it is a question.

i: "뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마"로 묻고 짧게 답하는 말입니다.
Ask with "뭐 (what), 어디 (where), 누구 (who), 언제 (when), 얼마 (how much)" and give short answers.
w: How much is it all together?
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
tp: 묻는 말은 끝을 올려서 말합니다. 대답은 짧게 해도 됩니다. "어디 가요?" "시장이요."
Raise your voice at the end of a question. Short answers are fine: "어디 가요?" (Where are you going?) "시장이요." (To the market.)
묻는 말은 영어처럼 문장 맨 앞에 오지 않고 보통 동사 앞에 옵니다. "뭐 먹어요?"
Question words do not come at the start of the sentence like in English. They usually come just before the verb: "뭐 먹어요?" (What are you eating?).
sm: "뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마"로 묻고, 대답은 짧게 합니다.
Ask with "뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마" and answer briefly.
qz: 값을 물을 때 쓰는 말은? 누구 / 얼마

i: 가족을 부르는 말입니다. 형제는 말하는 사람이 남자인지 여자인지에 따라 달라집니다.
Words for family members. The words for older brother and sister change depending on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
w: It was my father's birthday, so I made a video call.
(보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
My mother is a good cook.
My mother is sick, so I'm worried.
I send money to my parents.
I send living money to my parents every month.
My older brother is taller than me.
My older brother wants to study in Korea too.
My older brother is a university student.
I told my older brother the dates of my vacation.
to let someone know, to tell
My older sister is a nurse.
My older sister sent me wedding photos.
I live with my older sister.
My older sister bought me clothes.
My older sister helps me a lot with life in Korea.
My younger brother is a high school student.
I have two younger brothers and sisters.
I pay my younger sibling's school fees.
My grandfather is sick, so I took time off.
I'm going to my grandmother's house.
(보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
I bought Korean ginseng for my grandmother.
tp: English has only "brother" and "sister", but Korean has four words. A man says 형, 누나, and a woman says 오빠, 언니.
English has only "brother" and "sister", but Korean has four words for older siblings. A man says 형, 누나; a woman says 오빠, 언니.
동생은 남녀를 가리지 않습니다. 가릴 때는 남동생, 여동생이라고 합니다.
동생 is used for both boys and girls. To show which, say 남동생 (younger brother) or 여동생 (younger sister).
학교에서 친해지면 가족이 아니어도 나이 많은 선배나 친구를 형, 누나, 언니, 오빠라고 부릅니다.
When you become close at school, you can call older seniors or friends 형, 누나, 언니 or 오빠 even if they are not family.
dl: How many people are in your family?
다섯 명이에요. 부모님하고 누나, 동생이 있어요.
Five. I have my parents, an older sister and a younger brother.
daseot myeongieyo bumonimhago nuna, dongsaengi isseoyo
sm: 남자는 형과 누나, 여자는 오빠와 언니라고 부릅니다.
Men say 형 and 누나; women say 오빠 and 언니.
qz: 남자가 자기 "older sister"을 부르는 말은? 누나 / 언니

i: 결혼과 형제에 대해 말할 때 쓰는 낱말입니다.
Words for talking about marriage and brothers and sisters.
w: When do you want to get married?
My older sister got married last year.
My older brother is getting married in our hometown next year.
My older sister came to Korea with her husband.
누나가 남편 비자 서류를 준비하고 있어요.
nunaga nampyeon bija seoryureul junbihago isseoyo
My older sister is preparing her husband's visa documents.
My friend's wife is a good cook.
My senior's wife is in Nepal.
나중에 아내하고 세계 여행을 하고 싶어요.
najunge anaehago segye yeohaengeul hago sipeoyo
Someday I want to travel the world with my wife.
I'm the youngest son in my family.
My parents have only two sons.
My aunt's daughter goes to high school.
I'm an only daughter, so my parents worry a lot.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
I miss my brothers and sisters back home.
(보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
I have no brothers or sisters. I'm an only child.
to not have, to not be (there)
how many people in the family
How many people are in your family?
There are four people in my family.
Write on the form how many people are in your family.
tp: "결혼했어요"는 과거 모양이지만 "지금 결혼한 상태"라는 뜻입니다. 아직 안 했으면 "아직 안 했어요"라고 합니다.
"결혼했어요" is in the past form, but it means "I am married now". If you are not married yet, say "아직 안 했어요".
한국 사람은 처음 만나도 결혼했는지 자주 묻습니다. 실례로 생각하지 않아도 됩니다.
Koreans often ask if you are married, even the first time they meet you. You don't need to think it is rude.
dl: Sam, do you have any brothers or sisters?
Yes, I have one younger sister.
You must miss your younger sister.
(보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
sm: 결혼했는지는 "결혼했어요?"로 묻고 답합니다.
Ask and answer about marriage with "결혼했어요?".

i: 사람의 생김새를 말하는 낱말입니다.
Words for describing how people look.
w: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I got slimmer because I exercise these days.
The man in the photo is handsome.
The tall person is the teaching assistant.
키가 큰 사람이 위 칸을 정리해요.
kiga keun sarami wi kaneul jeongnihaeyo
The tall person tidies the top shelf.
키가 작아서 선반 위에 손이 안 닿아요.
kiga jagaseo seonban wie soni an daayo
I'm short, so I can't reach the top of the shelf.
My older sister and I look very alike.
My younger sibling looks a lot like me.
My older sister has long hair.
My hair is long, so I tie it up.
If your hair is long, tie it up when you cook.
tp: In English you say "tall" for a person, but Korean says "키가 크다" with the word "키" (height). "높다" (high) is not used for people.
In English you just say "tall", but Korean says "키가 크다", with the word "키" (height). "높다" (high) is not used for people.
"잘생겼어요", "닮았어요"는 과거 모양으로 지금의 모습을 말합니다.
"잘생겼어요" and "닮았어요" use the past form to talk about how someone looks now.
dl: What does your younger brother look like?
키가 크고 머리가 짧아요. 저를 닮았어요.
He is tall and has short hair. He looks like me.
kiga keugo meoriga jjalbayo jeoreul dalmasseoyo
sm: 사람의 키는 "크다, 작다"로 말합니다.
For a person's height, use "크다, 작다".

i: 사람의 성격을 말하는 낱말입니다. 학교에서 친구나 교수님을 소개할 때 나옵니다.
Words for describing a person's character. You hear them when people introduce friends or professors at school.
w: The staff at this shop are always kind.
My new roommate is nice, so I'm happy.
It's fun to chat with friends during the break.
The dormitory is quiet, so I sleep well.
My younger brother is outgoing and has many friends.
Outgoing people are good at welcoming customers.
to be right, to be correct
I'm hard-working, so I get up early.
I studied diligently, so I got praise.
If you are lazy, it is hard to extend your contract.
The shop owner is looking for a sincere part-timer.
My older sister is warm and caring.
Minha is warm to her friends.
tp: 한국 학교와 아르바이트 가게에서 가장 좋은 칭찬은 "성실하다"와 "부지런하다"입니다.
At Korean schools and part-time jobs, the best praise is "성실하다" and "부지런하다".
낱말 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 "-ㄴ/은"으로 바꿉니다. 친절한 사람, 조용한 방.
Before a noun, change it to "-ㄴ/은": 친절한 사람 (a kind person), 조용한 방 (a quiet room).
In English you say "She is kind" or "She is a kind person". In Korean, say "친절해요" or "친절한 사람이에요".
In English you say "She is kind" or "She is a kind person". In Korean, say "친절해요" or "친절한 사람이에요".
dl: He is very sincere and hard-working.
sm: 성격은 "-하다"로 끝나는 낱말이 많습니다.
Many character words end in "-하다".

i: 친구와 이웃, 사람을 사귀는 것에 대한 낱말입니다.
Words about friends, neighbors and making friends.
w: I joined this club because a friend introduced me.
I say hello to my neighbor.
My neighbor was noisy, so I couldn't sleep.
The two of them are dating.
I made a lot of friends.
I made friends at a Korean language group.
I watch a movie with my boyfriend.
My boyfriend is waiting in Bangladesh.
여자 친구 생일 선물을 골라 주세요.
yeoja chin-gu saengil seonmureul golla juseyo
Please help me choose a birthday present for my girlfriend.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I have a close friend in Korea.
I became close to my dorm roommate.
tp: 한국어의 "친구"는 보통 나이가 같은 사람입니다. 나이가 다르면 친해도 형, 누나, 동생이라고 부릅니다.
In Korean, "친구" usually means someone of the same age. If the age is different, even close people call each other 형, 누나, 동생.
"남자 친구", "여자 친구"는 애인이라는 뜻입니다. 그냥 친구는 "남자인 친구"처럼 풀어서 말합니다.
"남자 친구" and "여자 친구" mean boyfriend and girlfriend. For a friend who is just a friend, say "남자인 친구" (a friend who is a man).
dl: Let me introduce my friend Aisha.
Nice to meet you. Are you two close?
Yes, we are friends from the same hometown.
sm: "친구"는 나이가 같은 사이에 쓰는 말입니다.
"친구" is used between people of the same age.

i: 한국어에는 숫자가 두 가지 있습니다. 이 묶음은 날짜, 돈, 전화번호, 층, 분에 쓰는 "일, 이, 삼"입니다.
Korean has two sets of numbers. This set is "일, 이, 삼", used for dates, money, phone numbers, floors and minutes.
w: Please go up to the 2nd floor.
Please use the restroom on the 2nd floor.
I extend my visa in three months.
제 방은 육 층 육백이 호예요.
je bangeun yuk cheung yukpaegi hoyeyo
My room is room 602 on the 6th floor.
I get my part-time pay on the 7th of every month.
팔 번 버스가 학교 앞에 서요.
pal beon beoseuga hakkyo ape seoyo
Bus No. 8 stops in front of the school.
There is a test in September.
The last number of the phone number is nine.
We'll give you a ten percent discount.
tp: Numbers are made in a very regular way: 십일 (ten-one = 11), 이십 (two-ten = 20), 삼십오 (three-ten-five = 35). There are no special words like "eleven" or "twenty" in English.
Numbers are made in a regular way: 십일 (11 = ten-one), 이십 (20 = two-ten), 삼십오 (35 = three-ten-five). Unlike English "eleven" or "twenty", every number follows the rule.
Big numbers are grouped by "만" (10,000). 100,000 is "십만" and 1,000,000 is "백만". This is different from English, which groups by thousands.
Big numbers are counted in units of "만" (10,000). 100,000 is "십만" (ten 만), 1,000,000 is "백만" (a hundred 만). This is different from English, which groups by thousands.
전화번호는 한 자리씩 읽고, 0은 "공"이라고 합니다.
Read phone numbers one digit at a time, and say 0 as "공".
dl: What floor is the department office on?
sm: 날짜, 돈, 번호, 층, 분에는 "일, 이, 삼"을 씁니다.
For dates, money, numbers, floors and minutes, use "일, 이, 삼".

i: 물건이나 사람을 세고 시간과 나이를 말할 때 쓰는 "하나, 둘, 셋"입니다.
"하나, 둘, 셋" are used to count things and people, and to say the hour and age.
w: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
May I ask one more thing?
The two of us go together.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
The two of us lift this box together.
하나, 둘, 셋 하면 같이 들어요.
hana, dul, set hamyeon gachi deureoyo
When I say one, two, three, we lift it together.
Four of us share our room.
Do you have a table for five?
I eat dinner at six o'clock.
I get up at seven o'clock.
You must come to the library by seven o'clock.
I start my part-time job at eight o'clock.
I sleep eight hours a day.
The bank opens at nine o'clock.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I go to bed at ten o'clock.
Please be quiet after ten o'clock.
We have to move twenty boxes.
tp: 세는 말 앞에서 모양이 바뀝니다. 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네, 스물 → 스무. 한 개, 두 명, 세 시, 네 살, 스무 살.
Before a counter word, the form changes: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네, 스물 → 스무. 한 개, 두 명, 세 시, 네 살, 스무 살.
시각을 말할 때 "시"는 고유어 숫자, "분"은 한자어 숫자입니다. 세 시 십 분.
When telling the time, "시" uses native Korean numbers (하나, 둘…) and "분" uses Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이…): 세 시 십 분 (3:10).
dl: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)

tp: 버스와 지하철은 탈 때와 내릴 때 모두 교통카드를 찍습니다. 내릴 때 찍어야 갈아탈 때 돈을 덜 냅니다.
On buses and the subway, tap your card both when you get on and when you get off. You must tap when you get off to pay less when you transfer.
지하철 노선은 "일 호선, 이 호선"처럼 "일, 이, 삼" 숫자로 말합니다.
Subway lines use the numbers "일, 이, 삼": 일 호선, 이 호선.
dl: 시장에 가려면 몇 번 버스를 타요?
Which bus do I take to go to the market?
to ride, to get on (a car, boat)
sijange garyeomyeon myeot beon beoseureul tayo?
십이 번을 타고 시청 앞에서 내리세요.
Take bus number 12 and get off in front of City Hall.
to ride, to get on (a car, boat)
sibi beoneul tago sicheong apeseo naeriseyo
sm: 버스는 번호로, 지하철은 호선으로 말합니다.
Buses are called by number, and subway lines by 호선.

i: 날마다 가는 곳과 꼭 알아야 하는 곳의 이름입니다.
Names of places you go every day and places you must know.
w: I'll go to the restroom and come back.
Throw toilet paper into the toilet.
My home is close to school.
Please text me when you get home.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
What time does the library close?
I borrowed a book from the library.
I eat lunch at a restaurant.
The restaurant is full of people.
A Nepali person runs this restaurant.
Let's meet in front of City Hall.
City Hall gives counseling to foreigners.
There is a stationery store in front of the school.
On weekends, the school teaches Korean for free.
What time does the hospital open?
외국인도 갈 수 있는 병원이 있어요?
oegugindo gal su inneun byeongwoni isseoyo?
Is there a hospital that foreigners can go to?
I take out money at the bank.
I opened a student bank account at the bank.
It takes one hour to the airport.
Where do I take the airport bus?
to ride, to get on (a car, boat)
I reported it to the police station.
I lost my wallet, so I went to the police station.
I'm going to the Bangladeshi embassy.
The embassy is closed on weekends.
If you lose your passport, contact your embassy.
tp: 가는 곳에는 "에", 무엇을 하는 곳에는 "에서"를 붙입니다. 도서관에 가요. 도서관에서 공부해요.
Use "에" for the place you go to, and "에서" for the place where you do something: 도서관에 가요. 도서관에서 공부해요.
장소를 물을 때는 "~이/가 어디예요?"라고 합니다.
To ask about a place, say "~이/가 어디예요?".
pr: 도서관에 가다 to go to the library
도서관에서 공부하다 to study at the library
dl: I'm going to the bank. I send money at the bank.
sm: 가는 곳은 "에", 하는 곳은 "에서"입니다.
Use "에" for where you go, and "에서" for where you do something.

i: 얼마나 멀고 시간이 얼마나 걸리는지 말하는 낱말입니다.
Words for saying how far something is and how long it takes.
w: Where is the closest supermarket to the dormitory?
If it's too far, take a taxi.
to ride, to get on (a car, boat)
How much is a taxi to the airport?
The bus came late, so I was late for class.
A taxi is faster than a bus.
Processing the documents takes one week.
the road is jammed, traffic jam
There is a traffic jam in the morning.
There was a traffic jam, so I was late.
On Friday evenings, the traffic is very bad.
tp: 어디에서 어디까지는 "에서 ~까지", 언제부터 언제까지는 "부터 ~까지"입니다. 집에서 학교까지. 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지.
From one place to another, use "에서 ~까지"; from one time to another, use "부터 ~까지": 집에서 학교까지. 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지.
시간의 길이는 "분", "시간"으로 말합니다. "시"는 시각이고 "시간"은 길이입니다. 두 시(2 o'clock), 두 시간(2 hours).
For lengths of time, use "분" and "시간". "시" is the time on the clock, and "시간" is hours: 두 시 (2 o'clock), 두 시간 (2 hours).
dl: How long does it take from the dormitory to the library?
sm: 걸리는 시간은 "얼마나 걸려요?"로 묻습니다.
Ask how long it takes with "얼마나 걸려요?".

i: 집 안의 곳곳을 가리키는 낱말입니다.
Words for the different parts of a home.
w: 부엌은 같이 쓰니까 깨끗이 써 주세요.
bu-eokeun gachi sseunikka kkaekkeusi sseo juseyo
We share the kitchen, so please keep it clean.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
불이 나면 엘리베이터 말고 계단으로 가세요.
buri namyeon ellibe-iteo malgo gedaneuro gaseyo
If there is a fire, use the stairs, not the elevator.
I watch TV in the living room.
We all eat together in the living room.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
곰팡이가 생기지 않게 창문을 자주 여세요.
gompangiga saenggiji anke changmuneul jaju yeoseyo
Open the windows often so mold doesn't grow.
I take off my shoes in the entryway.
Please leave the package in front of the door.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
My room was cold, so I bought an electric heating pad.
The bathroom is next to the room.
tp: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗고 들어갑니다. 바닥에 난방이 들어와서 겨울에도 바닥이 따뜻합니다.
In Korean homes, you take off your shoes at the entryway. The floor is heated, so it is warm even in winter.
한국 화장실은 보통 샤워하는 곳과 같이 있습니다.
In Korea, the bathroom and the shower are usually in the same room.
dl: There is one room and one kitchen.
Yes, it's next to the entryway.
sm: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗습니다.
In Korean homes, you take off your shoes at the 현관.

i: 방에 있는 가구와 전기 제품의 이름입니다.
Names of furniture and electrical appliances in a room.
w: 침대 시트를 일주일에 한 번 빨아요.
chimdae siteureul ilju-ire han beon pparayo
I wash the bed sheets once a week.
The chair is broken. Please change it.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I study Korean at my desk.
I put my clothes in the wardrobe.
The wardrobe door doesn't close well.
Please put it in the refrigerator.
There is milk in the refrigerator.
Write your name on the food you put in the refrigerator.
Use the washing machine only until 10 p.m.
Please turn on the air conditioner.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
The air conditioner is too cold.
Turn on the air conditioner and close the windows.
Turn off the fan when you go out.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I watch Korean news on TV.
tp: 전기 제품은 "켜다", "끄다"를 씁니다. 문과 창문의 "열다", "닫다"와 다릅니다. 영어도 "turn on, turn off"와 "open, close"로 나눕니다.
For electrical appliances, use "켜다" and "끄다". They are different from "열다" and "닫다" for doors and windows. English is the same: "turn on, turn off" and "open, close".
가전제품 이름에는 "-기"가 자주 붙습니다. 세탁기, 선풍기, 청소기.
Names of home appliances often end in "-기": 세탁기, 선풍기, 청소기 (vacuum cleaner).
dl: 침대, 옷장, 에어컨이 있어요. 세탁기는 일 층에 있어요.
There is a bed, a wardrobe and an air conditioner. The washing machine is on the first floor.
chimdae, otjang, e-eokeoni isseoyo setakkineun il cheunge isseoyo
sm: 전기 제품은 "켜다, 끄다"를 씁니다.
For electrical appliances, use "켜다, 끄다".

i: 집과 기숙사에서 하는 일을 말하는 동사입니다.
Verbs for the chores you do at home and in the dormitory.
w: We take turns cleaning the room.
I do the laundry on Sunday.
이사 가기 전에 기숙사 방을 정리하세요.
isa gagi jeone gisuksa bangeul jeongnihaseyo
Tidy your dorm room before you move out.
Some water spilled. Please wipe the floor.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
I wash the dishes after eating.
Wash your dishes right after you eat.
I take out the trash at night.
Food waste must be thrown away separately.
tp: 한국에서는 쓰레기를 나누어 버립니다. 일반 쓰레기는 돈을 내고 사는 봉투에 넣어야 합니다.
In Korea, you sort your trash. General trash must go in special bags that you buy.
"씻다"는 물로 몸이나 물건을 씻을 때, "닦다"는 문질러서 깨끗하게 할 때 씁니다. 이는 "닦다"를 씁니다.
"씻다" is for washing with water, and "닦다" is for wiping or rubbing clean. For teeth, use "이를 닦다" (to brush your teeth).
dl: 제가 청소할게요. 아이샤 씨는 쓰레기를 버려 주세요.
I'll clean. Aisha, please take out the trash.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
jega cheongsohalgeyo a-isya ssineun sseuregireul beoryeo juseyo
sm: 집안일은 "-하다"로 끝나는 낱말이 많습니다.
Many words for housework end in "-하다".

i: 학교 기숙사에서 여러 사람과 함께 살 때 필요한 낱말입니다.
Words you need when you live with many people in a university dormitory.
w: There are a lot of rules.
규칙을 안 지키면 기숙사에서 나가야 해요.
gyuchigeul an jikimyeon gisuksa-eseo nagaya haeyo
If you don't follow the rules, you have to leave the dormitory.
I live in the university dormitory.
The dormitory is next to the library.
I pay the dormitory fee every semester.
I do my laundry in the laundry room.
The laundry room is on the first floor.
Don't leave your laundry in the laundry room for a long time.
It's warm when you turn on the heating.
If the heating breaks, tell the manager.
to come out, to happen (열이 나다 = to have a fever)
Please turn on the air conditioning.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
The air conditioning is too strong.
냉방을 너무 세게 하면 감기에 걸려요.
naengbangeul neomu sege hamyeon gamgie geollyeoyo
If the air conditioning is too strong, you'll catch a cold.
Put shared things back in their place.
The shower room is at the end of the hallway.
There is no hot water in the shower room.
The shower room is crowded in the morning.
My roommate is sleeping, so I'm quiet.
시험 기간이니까 밤에도 조용히 해 주세요.
siheom giganinikka bamedo joyonghi hae juseyo
It's exam period, so please be quiet at night too.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
tp: 기숙사에 문제가 있으면 "~이/가 안 돼요", "~이/가 고장 났어요"라고 관리인에게 말합니다.
If there is a problem in the dormitory, tell the manager "~이/가 안 돼요" (doesn't work) or "~이/가 고장 났어요" (is broken).
한국 겨울은 영하로 내려갑니다. 난방이 안 되면 바로 말해야 합니다.
Korean winters go below zero. If the heating doesn't work, tell someone right away.
장소 이름에는 "-실"이 자주 붙습니다. 샤워실, 세탁실, 휴게실.
Place names often end in "-실" (room): 샤워실, 세탁실, 휴게실 (break room).
dl: The heating in my room doesn't work.
to know (알겠어요 = I understand, got it)
sm: 문제가 있으면 "~이/가 안 돼요"라고 말합니다.
If there's a problem, say "~이/가 안 돼요".

i: 방을 구하고 계약할 때 나오는 낱말입니다. 한국에는 "보증금"이라는 큰돈이 있습니다.
Words for finding a room and signing a contract. In Korea there is a large sum of money called "보증금".
w: I asked the landlord to repair it.
to look for (a room, a job)
How much is the monthly rent for a studio?
Studios near the station are expensive.
How much is the monthly rent?
I pay the rent by the 5th of every month.
You get the deposit back when you move out.
When you move, you must report your new address.
Be sure to see the room before you sign the contract.
Is the internet included in the maintenance fee?
In winter, the maintenance fee is high.
tp: 보증금은 들어갈 때 맡기고 나올 때 돌려받는 돈입니다. 월세의 열 배가 넘을 때도 있습니다.
A 보증금 is money you leave when you move in and get back when you move out. Sometimes it is more than ten times the monthly rent.
계약서는 꼭 받아서 가지고 있어야 합니다. 모르는 말이 있으면 서명하기 전에 물어봅니다.
Be sure to get a copy of the contract and keep it. If there are words you don't understand, ask before you sign.
dl: How much is the monthly rent for this studio?
보증금 삼백만 원에 월세 삼십오만 원이에요.
The deposit is 3,000,000 won and the monthly rent is 350,000 won.
bojeunggeum sambaengman wone wolse samsiboman wonieyo
Is there a maintenance fee too?
sm: 방을 구할 때는 보증금, 월세, 관리비를 모두 묻습니다.
When you look for a room, ask about the 보증금, 월세 and 관리비.

i: 날마다 쓰는 물건의 이름입니다. 한국에 처음 가면 가장 먼저 사야 하는 것들입니다.
Names of things you use every day. These are the first things to buy when you arrive in Korea.
w: I dry myself with a towel.
to not have, there is no
I wash my hands with soap.
The hand soap has run out.
I bought shampoo and conditioner together.
Toothpaste and toothbrushes are cheap at Daiso.
Pack your toothbrush when you go on a business trip.
The toilet paper has run out.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
There is no toilet paper in the bathroom.
to not have, there is no
Please give me one more pillow.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
The pillow is hard, so my neck hurts.
Put in only a little detergent.
The detergent in the laundry room has run out.
빨래, 설거지 할 때 쓰는 것
tp: 물건이 다 없어졌을 때는 "떨어졌어요"라고 합니다. 휴지가 떨어졌어요.
When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요": 휴지가 떨어졌어요 (The toilet paper has run out).
한국에서는 휴지를 변기에 버립니다. 집들이 선물로도 휴지를 줍니다.
In Korea, you throw toilet paper into the toilet. People also give toilet paper as a housewarming gift.
dl: I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?
Please buy me some toothpaste and toilet paper.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
sm: 물건이 다 없어지면 "떨어졌어요"라고 합니다.
When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요".
qz: The toilet paper has run out.

i: 몸의 여러 곳의 이름입니다. 아플 때와 다쳤을 때 꼭 필요합니다.
Names of parts of the body. You need them when you are sick or hurt.
w: I got dust in my eye.
If the smell is strong, cover your nose with a mask.
I have sores in my mouth, so I can't eat.
My roommate snores, so I wear earplugs.
to be dry (목이 마르다 = to be thirsty)
My throat hurts, so I can't talk.
I put a pain relief patch on my shoulder.
I wash my hands before I eat.
I have a stomachache, so I go to the bathroom often.
I lifted something heavy and hurt my back.
Be careful of your back when you lift things.
My leg hurts, so I can't walk.
I stood for a long time, so my legs are swollen.
Something heavy fell on my foot.
tp: 아픈 곳은 "~이/가 아파요"로 말합니다. 순서가 영어와 같습니다. "My head hurts" = 머리가 아파요.
Say where it hurts with "~이/가 아파요". The order is the same as English: "My head hurts" = 머리가 아파요.
"머리"는 "head"와 "hair" 두 가지 뜻입니다. 머리를 감다(wash your hair), 머리를 자르다(get a haircut).
"머리" has two meanings: head and hair. 머리를 감다 (to wash your hair), 머리를 자르다 (to get a haircut).
눈(eye, snow), 배(stomach, boat, pear), 다리(leg, bridge)는 뜻이 여럿입니다.
눈 (eye, snow), 배 (stomach, boat, pear) and 다리 (leg, bridge) have more than one meaning.
sm: 아픈 곳은 "몸의 이름 + 이/가 아파요"로 말합니다.
Say where it hurts with "body part + 이/가 아파요".

i: 몸이 어떻게 아픈지 말하는 표현입니다.
Expressions for saying how you feel sick.
w: If you're sick, don't just put up with it. Tell someone.
to put up with, to hold back
Be careful not to catch a cold.
감기에 걸려서 오늘 수업에 못 가요.
gamgie geollyeoseo oneul su-eobe mot gayo
I caught a cold, so I can't go to class today.
I had a fever at night.
열이 나면 학교에 가지 말고 병원에 가세요.
yeori namyeon hakkyo-e gaji malgo byeongwone gaseyo
If you have a fever, don't go to school. Go to the hospital.
I studied a lot for the exam, so I'm tired.
I ate bad food and got an upset stomach.
I had an upset stomach, so I ate rice porridge.
I caught a cold, so I have a runny nose.
If you have a runny nose, wear a mask.
I coughed at night, so I couldn't sleep.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
If you feel dizzy, sit down.
I walked for a long time on a hot day, so I feel dizzy.
I think I'm going to throw up.
I ate bad food and threw up.
tp: 증상은 "나다"로 많이 말합니다. 열이 나다, 콧물이 나다, 피가 나다. 몸에서 밖으로 나온다는 뜻입니다.
Symptoms often use "나다": 열이 나다, 콧물이 나다, 피가 나다. It means something comes out of the body.
병에는 "걸리다"를 씁니다. 지금 아파도 "걸렸어요"처럼 과거 모양으로 말합니다.
Use "걸리다" for illnesses. Even if you are still sick now, use the past form "걸렸어요".
아프면 참지 말고 "몸이 안 좋아요"라고 교수님께 말합니다.
If you're sick, don't put up with it. Tell your professor "몸이 안 좋아요" (I don't feel well).
pr: 아프다 to hurt, to be sick
감기에 걸리다 to catch a cold
감기가 낫다 to get over a cold
dl: 샘 씨, 얼굴이 안 좋아요. 어디 아파요?
Sam, you don't look well. Are you sick?
saem ssi, eolguri an joayo eodi apayo?
감기에 걸렸어요. 열이 나고 기침을 해요.
I caught a cold. I have a fever and a cough.
gamgie geollyeosseoyo yeori nago gichimeul haeyo
to try, to have done (-아/어 보다)
sm: 증상은 "~이/가 나다", 병은 "~에 걸리다"로 말합니다.
For symptoms, say "~이/가 나다"; for illnesses, say "~에 걸리다".

i: 병원에서 접수하고 진료받을 때 듣는 낱말입니다.
Words you hear when you check in and see a doctor at a hospital.
w: I have to go to the hospital.
I saw a doctor at the hospital.
병원에 갈 때 외국인 등록증을 가져가세요.
byeongwone gal ttae oegugin deungnokjeungeul gajeogaseyo
Take your alien registration card when you go to the hospital.
의사 선생님께 아픈 곳을 보여 주세요.
uisa seonsaengnimkke apeun goseul boyeo juseyo
Show the doctor where it hurts.
to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
The nurse checked my blood pressure.
Show your health insurance card when you check in.
Don't eat anything tomorrow morning and come for the test.
I was in the hospital for three days.
to be admitted to the hospital
I have to stay in the hospital for surgery.
to be admitted to the hospital
If you are in the hospital, give a doctor's note to the school.
to be admitted to the hospital
You have to wait to see the doctor.
On Saturdays, the clinic is open only in the morning.
If you have health insurance, hospital bills are cheap.
tp: 병원에 갈 때는 외국인등록증과 건강보험증을 가져갑니다.
When you go to the hospital, take your alien registration card and health insurance card.
한국에서는 가벼운 병이면 큰 병원이 아니라 동네 의원에 먼저 갑니다. 내과, 정형외과, 치과처럼 아픈 곳에 따라 나뉩니다.

In Korea, if you are not very sick, you go to a local clinic first, not a big hospital. Clinics are divided by the part that hurts, such as 내과 (internal medicine), 정형외과 (orthopedics, bones) and 치과 (dentist).
주사는 "맞다"를 씁니다. 주사를 맞다.

To open a bank account, take your ID to the bank.
